scope_note: All tracked modules receive a lexical inventory; the groups below are manual API triage, not a claim of exhaustive semantic equivalence. No file is removed merely because it has no in-repository import.

integration_limitations.reproduction: tests/test_extra_monoid.nim has imports nested in a when block; the embed ImportExpand call is emitted at column zero and the following indented proc fails parsing on both required Nim versions.
integration_limitations.baseline: expander.py, test_extra_monoid.nim and the restored monoid.nim are byte-identical to HEAD. Direct, plain and bundle modes pass; non-conditional public-contract fixtures pass all four modes.
integration_limitations.action: Separate expander regression/fix before extending embed coverage to conditional-import inputs; do not change the monoid API to work around it.

groups.reason: Keep both public APIs; their ordering engine is already shared.
The legacy wrapper delegates to the canonical matcher. Preserve empty-pattern semantics and both import orders.
The P1 iterative low-link traversal is shared. Keep adapters and result ordering.

Legacy encode keeps c/n tuple fields and delegates to runLengthEncode. Canonical string encoding delegates to its generic core. Keep legacy decoders: string elements concatenate within a run, and negative counts raise RangeDefect rather than AssertionDefect.
Share sorting/deduplication and lookups, but preserve the legacy sequence representation, variadic constructor, mutating build and missing-key assertion.
groups.required_tests: Legacy direct import, both import orders, empty input, multiple pools, custom ordered values, missing keys and sequence operations.

groups.reason: The backup exposes a matching entry point but uses specialized FFT logic. The slow version additionally exports ProductTree helpers; it cannot simply be deleted.
groups.required_tests: Horner oracle; empty polynomial and points; repeated points; non-power-of-two lengths; supported moduli and coefficient types; ProductTree helper consumers.

groups.reason: Fixed immutable, dynamically expanding var, and compile-time/static contracts differ. Re-exporting the dynamic API would break let-bound legacy consumers.
Legacy SA_Node references, generic automaton type, int32 indices and mutable exposed nodes differ from canonical value states and occurrence lifecycle.
The current range hash is a length-aware PartialRollingHash; the old one returns RH and exposes different connect/base operations. Do not alias result types.
Legacy Graph is a sequence; newer containers have object, directedness, callback or CSR contracts. Shared adapters must preserve sequence operations and reverse-edge conventions.
Legacy arbitrary roots and asymmetric directional edge weights must map to the newer iterative engine; callback argument semantics are not interchangeable.
The main legacy facade already uses the canonical compressed tree. The backup also exports recursive/internal-parameter methods and a different object type.
Value-only, action-only, lazy and position-dependent actions, plus stored versus static callbacks, require a full API matrix before replacement.
set_map is already a facade. Red-black, splay and randomized backends have different node, iterator and balancing contracts.
Allocation/traversal helpers are already shared; aggregate and dual-update operations remain different.
math/int128 is already a compatibility facade. Integer and floating-point widths have distinct range, rounding and ABI contracts; internal limb operations are shared.
Divide-and-conquer already re-exports monotoneMinima. SMAWK assumes total monotonicity and is not an unconditional replacement.
The functional-name alias already delegates to Chu-Liu/Edmonds.

Legacy fragments and overlapping implementations are candidates, not proven removable files. Confirm exported routines, include-style use, status enums and numeric contracts before adapting each family.
Export visibility, supported shapes, string/ptr handling and overload fallback differ. Macro text similarity does not establish compatibility.
The four-tree rectangle-add/prefix-sum equations are duplicated; dense versus sparse storage must remain separate. Extract the arithmetic/update kernel without merging public types or include guards.
groups.required_tests: Existing coexistence test and both range Fenwick contracts, both import orders, empty boundaries, random grid oracle and custom additive/scalar types.

groups.reason: Many butterfly loops are copied, but root initialization differs: ACL mod/primitive_root versus the universal get_pow2_root extension point. Share loop kernels only after coefficient and root-policy coverage.

Residual storage and shortest augmenting path code overlap. The generalized graph has graphType policies and negative-cost initialization; the ACL API asserts nonnegative added costs. Preserve those policies and reset/set_edge APIs.
Event lifecycle and rectangle validation overlap, but point queries and rectangle coefficient integration require different kernels and output semantics.
Shared-looking arithmetic fragments do not imply equivalent precision, rounding, ownership or GMP/MPFR FFI contracts. External dependencies also require a dedicated validation environment.
Exported mutable nodes, parent pointers, lazy callbacks and position-dependent actions differ. An old filename and absence of local imports do not authorize breaking external consumers.
Legacy permutation/combination iterators delegate to itertools; unrelated nth_element and setUnion routines remain in algorithmutils.

new_algorithm_candidates.new_capability: Directed root-to-vertex path domination; SCC and undirected articulation do not answer it.
new_algorithm_candidates.required_tests: Unreachable vertices, loops, parallel arcs, vertex-deletion reachability oracle on small directed graphs, deep chains.

new_algorithm_candidates.new_capability: All-pairs undirected minimum-cut queries through a cut-equivalent tree; reuse the existing flow engine.
new_algorithm_candidates.required_tests: Compare every pair with fresh maxflow calls; disconnected graphs, zero capacities, parallel edges and wide capacity values.

new_algorithm_candidates.new_capability: Weighted non-bipartite matching; the existing general matcher is unweighted and Hungarian handles bipartite assignment.
new_algorithm_candidates.required_tests: Subset-DP oracle on small graphs, odd cycles, negative and zero weights, explicit cardinality tie policy. Higher implementation and verification cost; defer until existing legacy audits are complete.
